item.title: Automatically turn off idle screen with LXC GPU passthrough on LXC restart
item.author: invalid@example.com (ajeun)
item.dc:creator: ajeun
item.content:encoded:
I am using GPU passthrough to LXC on proxmox running on a laptop and don't want the screen always on so I set `consoleblank=30`:

```
# /etc/kernel/cmdline
root=ZFS=rpool/ROOT/pve-1 boot=zfs intel_iommu=on iommu=pt consoleblank=30
```


This seems to work correctly without any LXCs running. The computer boots up and after 30 seconds the screen turns off as expected.

Now I added an LXC with GPU passthrough for running frigate. Frigate works fine and on boot the screen works as expected...

item.title: After a ransomware hit, how do you check PBS snapshots for signs of compromise before restoring?
item.author: invalid@example.com (UriShay-CyberSnap)
item.dc:creator: UriShay-CyberSnap
item.content:encoded:
Question for people who've had to restore VMs after an incident. Verify jobs tell you the chunks are intact, but they don't tell you if the attacker was already inside the guest when the backup ran. How are you deciding how far back to go? Mounting old snapshots in an isolated VM and scanning, checking file changes between snapshots, something else? Curious what actually works at scale with dozens of VMs.

Disclosure: I'm the founder of CyberSnap, which does snapshot compromise checks.
